newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Finance Inspectorate says broker broke law.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Finance Inspectorate says broker broke law.

text.p: The Swedish Finance Inspectorate said on Monday one of the country's biggest brokerage houses had broken the law on securities operations between 1994 and 1996.
The state watchdog said D. Carnegie AB had failed to "take into account ethical considerations" in business deals and lending operations.
But the watchdog said Carnegie had instituted several changes to strengthen monitoring operations at the brokerage and that a warning would be sufficient.

"Carnegie took part in business deals that do not adhere to normal commercial and business practices, partly through the way Carnegie evaded market and counterparty risk," the Inspectorate said in a statement.
In addition, Carnegie had not planned to register loans with the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
"The investigation raised questions of an ethical character and show that Carnegie did not have sufficiently well-functioning procedures to take into account ethical considerations.
"The Finance Inspectorate finds that Carnegie thus broke Chapter 1 Paragraph 7 of the law on securities operations," it added.

But it said that Carnegie had acknowledged its faults and taken action. "Through these measures, Carnegie showed a clear ambition to, in the future, avoid situations similar to those that emerged in the investigation," the Inspectorate said,

Carnegie's board of directors had been strengthened with two external members, a new compliance function had been introduced and Carnegie had pledged to improve business ethics training, the watchdog added.
Carnegie was not immediately available for comment. -- Simon Haydon, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1004
